# Public synthetic numerical regression

`reference.json` is a reviewed numerical expectation for Issue #10. It was
generated by the real acquisition, shared QA, extraction, grouped evaluation,
immutable prediction and validated report pipeline in the verified environment
defined in `environment/reference.json`. Its generation environment, wheel and
native-library evidence, code identity, algorithm-file hashes and input digest
are archived in the file. The expected observations are never rewritten by the
validation command or CI.

## Workload and interpretation

The fixed generator uses seed `1092026`, three synthetic subject IDs (`001`,
`1`, `NA`), and two separately identified sessions per subject. Each session
contains 44 seconds of eight-channel data sampled at 500 Hz, UTC events, trial
eligibility, a rest-epoch manifest, and acquisition metadata. Four rest and four
task epochs per session give 48 epochs. Every value is synthetic; no private
raw recordings are needed or recovered.

Extraction retains the historical seven analysis channels and six frequency
bands: all 168 baseline BP/COH features and all 144 extension asymmetry/PLV
features are produced. To keep public CI bounded, the baseline evaluation uses
the prespecified `BP__FP1__alpha`, `BP__FP2__alpha` and
`COH__FP1__FP2__alpha` columns; a second experiment uses
`PLV__FP1__FP2__alpha`. SFS selects at most one feature, and each RBF search has
one C/gamma pair. LDA, RBF-SVM and KFDA run actual outer leave-one-subject-out
and inner leave-one-training-subject-out evaluation. Both sessions of a held-out
subject stay outside every fit. The result contains 18 classifier-fold rows and
288 predictions across the two experiments.

This is a grouped-CV software regression. Its accuracy is neither an estimate
from the private study nor fixed-model external validation; Issue #11's separate
fit/predict/score lifecycle is not implemented by this fixture. Runtime is about
seven seconds on the reference development runner, including environment
verification; machine and filesystem speed can change that figure.

## Numerical acceptance criteria

| Evidence | Acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Subject/session/epoch keys, feature order, selected features, fold and prediction coverage, true labels | Exact semantic equality |
| Mean, population standard deviation, minimum and maximum of every baseline and extension column; all epoch values for six declared baseline and five extension sentinels | `abs(actual - expected) <= 1e-10 + 1e-8 * abs(expected)` |
| Predicted labels and per-fold accuracy | Exact numerical equality |
| Subject-mean accuracy, sample standard deviation and pooled accuracy in summaries | `rtol=1e-12`, `atol=1e-14` for floating aggregation |
| Complete evaluation and report artifacts | Existing validators recompute coverage, selected-feature indices, fold accuracy and report arithmetic; hashes alone are insufficient |

Feature tolerances allow small floating-point differences in filtering, FFTs,
Hilbert transforms and feature reductions. They are fixed review decisions,
not intervals fitted to a proposed dependency upgrade. Summary tolerances only
allow aggregation roundoff; the existing validator independently checks exact
subject counts and prediction identities. Cross-environment feature CSV byte
equality is not required. Raw source bytes are hash-bound when comparing two
environments so both pipelines receive identical input.

## Run and inspect

After installing the reference environment and setting its documented thread
variables and `EEG_MA_INSTALL_REPORT`:

```sh
python scripts/19_validate_numerics.py \
  --out-dir outputs/numerics-reference \
  --require-reference-environment
```

The immutable directory contains `raw/`, `features/baseline/`,
`features/extensions/`, the existing `evaluation/` run and report manifests,
and `numerical_report.json`. The report includes actual environment evidence,
source/input/config/reference identities, observed numbers, per-field maximum
absolute differences, explicit tolerances and validation status. It embeds the
reviewed reference so archived comparisons can be recomputed without relying
on a later checkout's reference file.

Compatibility checks run the same command without
`--require-reference-environment`; they use the same numerical criteria and
record their actual environment. This does not certify that environment as the
reference. Numerical drift returns exit code 2 and saves complete diagnostic
evidence. Structural failures return a blocked error and never publish a
successful output directory. Existing output directories are never overwritten.

For a controlled dependency comparison, run the same analysis checkout in the
candidate environment:

```sh
python scripts/19_validate_numerics.py \
  --out-dir outputs/numerics-candidate \
  --environment-spec /path/to/candidate/environment/reference.json \
  --require-reference-environment \
  --compare-to outputs/numerics-reference/numerical_report.json
```

The comparison first validates the baseline report and its complete raw file
inventory, then reuses those exact raw bytes. It requires identical analysis
source, fixture/config, input and reviewed numerical-reference identities;
environment-only differences are expected. A candidate must satisfy both the
committed reference and the baseline comparison with unchanged tolerances.
The candidate report embeds the baseline report and recomputes both comparison
branches during validation; rehashing contradictory status, metrics or
environment identities cannot make them valid.

Changes to expected results require a separately reviewed fixture change and
evidence from a verified reference environment. There is no update/bless flag.
Inspect the scientific reason, feature/identity differences and downstream
predictions before proposing such a change; a dependency candidate never
updates expected values automatically.
